success_patterns: Verbatim clue recall: in 4 of 8 tasks (Carpathia, Sherbet, Bull Moose, Lenin) the clue or a near-copy appeared in the passages and the answer was read straight from it. The existing Rule 3 already covers this, so it should stay unchanged.

The agent named the slot type first (person, ship, raft, fruit crop) and answered with one bare entity of that type, such as Earl Warren, John Fogerty, Kon-Tiki or Bananas. The agent never answered with an anchor from the clue or a related entity. Rules 2 and 4 already cover this.

When the only verbatim-clue passages carried no answer (a PDF ad listing the clue, a quiz-spam page, a search-index page titled 'lenin - Search-ID'), the agent did not give up or guess. It used the page title or heading as a hint and corroborated it with topical passages repeating the clue's distinctive details (1992 stamp, 29-cent, Warren). It confirmed the result with its own knowledge. This is not yet in the skill.

The agent stripped clue words and type words from the final answer (Bull Moose rather than Bull Moose Party, Kon-Tiki rather than Kon-Tiki raft) and kept the plural for a crop (Bananas). Rule 4 already covers this.

patch.reasoning: Most of the batch's success is already encoded: verbatim archive copy, slot typing, and bare-form trimming. The one uncovered recurring behavior is how to treat a passage that repeats the clue but shows no answer. Such passages sometimes carry the answer in a title, heading or URL slug, and the agent also corroborated across topical passages and its own knowledge. This is a small procedural addition under Rule 3, not another example bullet, and it does not weaken verbatim-answer precedence.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - A passage that only REPEATS the clue with no answer after it (quiz-spam page, PDF ad list, search-index page) is not an archive hit, but its title, heading or URL slug often names the answer topic ('lenin - Search-ID'). Use that as a hint, then confirm it against the topical passages and your own knowledge. Answer the entity that recurs beside the clue's distinctive details (year, place, number, role), not a one-off mention.
